_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for UNP retrospectives (retro/build_unp.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history), the latest guide for the current fiscal year published by AS_OF, the latest dividend declaration, and the events published between that vintage and AS_OF. Union Pacific gives its numeric outlook in the 10-K ('Outlook' in Item 7) and in occasional 8-Ks, not in the quarterly releases, so guides are their own dated list. Values are as reported (no restatements), per share as traded on the day (before the 2008 and 2014 2:1 splits). EPS is diluted EPS from continuing operations; a company-published figure excluding a one-off replaces GAAP for that year. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time). Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing. A stock split ('splits') restates per-share facts published before its effective date (the first day the shares trade on the new basis) for every as-of date on or after it: per-share values are divided by the ratio and share counts multiplied by it. From Q1 2008 the company reports 'freight revenue' in place of 'commodity revenue' (prior periods reclassified); the fields commodity_revenue_b and commodity_pct hold whichever line the print reports, named by revenue_line. A vintage that follows a split may take years from filings published before it: eps_published and shares_published give those years' own publication dates, so the split restates exactly them. An 8-K that re-presents the 10-K's financial statements retrospectively (UNP's rail grinding accounting change, 2010-10-25) is a history vintage of its own from its date: it is the latest filing that reports those years.
